recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-13300; future registry-content defects should be addressed through the current external terminology governance/source path.
issue_request: FHIR-13300 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and reported that source/namingsystem/namingsystem-registry.xml had two entries whose NamingSystem resources both used id us-ssn; the Medicare entry should have used us-medicare.
initial_application: The issue was applied by svn revision 12609, now git commit ae17b6dedb88d7f0bcecd9bdcebce023a07f49f5, which changed the old us-medicare NamingSystem entry id from us-ssn to us-medicare. The Jira comment records that same revision.
additional_context: FHIR-16002 later reported the same duplicate-id problem and was marked Published/Persuasive with comments saying it was already fixed. FHIR-37889 later removed the old NamingSystem registry bundles from core examples because the content is maintained in HL7 Terminology.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The historical fix exactly matches FHIR-13300's request, and current source no longer includes the obsolete registry bundle where the duplicate existed.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive report of the same us-ssn/us-medicare duplicate, resolved as already fixed.
Later Published/Persuasive issue that removed the old core NamingSystem registry bundles because the content belongs in HL7 Terminology.
